messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert firing: SYNTH_CANARY: eu-west-1 prober returned 5xx rate 12% over 2m for probe 'canary-eu1-auth' (probe-id: a1b2c3). Auto-escalation to oncall-rotation.
pagerduty: PD Event: INC-40291: summary=\"SYNTH_CANARY canary-eu1-auth 5xx spike\". Triggered by metric threshold.
Sanjay K: got it, oncall-rotation is me this window. pulling up dashboards.
Maria G: I can help. Is this affecting production traffic or just the synth probes?
Sanjay K: looks like only synthetic checks for now. No customer-facing errors in prod logs but latency for auth microservice spiked in the EU region around same time.
Alice R: seeing a few transient 502s in the auth pod logs:
```
2024-11-09T15:12:03Z auth-svc-7f8c: http2 reset, upstream connection refused
2024-11-09T15:12:05Z auth-svc-7f8c: 502 response to /v1/token
```
Sanjay K: can someone check the prober fanout? I suspect duplicate firings from two prober workers. We had a similar dedupe-window bug last month.
Ops-bot: Canary prober group status: worker-a (ok), worker-b (ok), worker-c (restarted 15m ago), fanout_count=3, recent_runs=120.
Sanjay K: @Ops-bot any probe id duplication?
Ops-bot: Found 2 probe executions with identical probe-id header due to race in scheduler: run_ids a1b2c3 and a1b2c3 (dup). First run returned 502, second retried immediately -> caused double page.
Maria G: oh that explains the duplicate PagerDuty events. PD dedupe didn't catch because run_id was same but timestamp different?
Sanjay K: PD dedupe is keyed by check_name+region+run_id but our scheduler sometimes emits run_id twice within 30s window. PD dedupe TTL is 60s but the second event arrived after dedupe window due to queueing.
Alice R: For immediate mitigation can we silence the PD rule for SYNTH_CANARY in eu-west-1 for 10m? we don't want noisy pages while we fix the scheduler.
Sanjay K: /pd silence INC-40291 10m -- doing now.
oncall-rotation: Ack received by oncall-rotation (Sanjay K) for INC-40291.
pagerduty: Note: manual silence applied to rule SYNTH_CANARY eu-west-1 by Sanjay K for 10 minutes.
Maria G: I'll open a temporary probe-suppression flag to stop fanout >1. Deploying a toggle to disable worker retries.
Sanjay K: good. Also please post the mitigation command here so compliance has a record.
Maria G: mitigation: set /config/canary/fanout_override=1 via ops-config; rollout v2 -> commands:
```
ops-config apply --path /canary/fanout_override --value 1 --env eu-west-1
```
Maria G: applied. Waiting 30s to observe.
Alice R: after suppression the prober run count dropped to 1 per interval. No new PD events for 2m.
Ops-bot: Confirmed fanout_override=1 active in eu-west-1.
Sanjay K: great. Can we mark incident as "mitigated - noisy pages" and continue investigating root cause? I'm going to handoff to morning oncall in 15m.
Maria G: agree. I'll start a postmortem draft and add logs + scheduler trace. Suspect root cause: race in scheduler mark-done path not idempotent.
Alice R: I dug into the scheduler: when worker-c restarted it re-queued active tasks without revoking previous lease. A fix will be to add run-token check before enqueue.
Sanjay K: estimated impact: internal synth pages ~8 duplicates, customer impact = low (no user-facing errors seen), potential risk = transient auth latency.
pagerduty: PD Note: alert INC-40291 updated status -> Mitigated (silenced).
oncall-rotation: Handoff: @oncall-rotation (Sanjay K) -> @next_oncall (Maria G) in 15m. Sanjay will leave postmortem notes in #incidents-pm.
Sanjay K: adding action items: (1) hotfix scheduler dedupe v1 (2) add stronger PD dedupe keying (3) extend PD dedupe TTL for synth rules to 300s (4) automated suppression toggle in console UI.
Maria G: assigning tasks in tracker: SCHED-312 (hotfix), MON-204 (dedeupe TTL), UI-489 (suppression toggle).
Alice R: tests: load-replay with worker restart to validate no duplicate run_ids.
Ops-bot: runbook updated: section 'synth-noisy-pages' added with steps to silence PD, apply fanout_override, and notify cust-success if user impact observed.
Sanjay K: closing thread in 30m if no further pages. Thanks all :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Thread closed by incident-bot (no new activity).
